purpose: Observed evidence that the Pulso web drives its isotype with exactly two inputs — a named zone pose and a local progress number — which the approved Isotipo3D contract already exposes as `scene` and `progress`. notCaptured.reason: The web blends two pose families and moves the logo between anchor slots (`mix: { a, b, t }` in pulso-iso3d.mjs, band logic in pulso-director.js). Reproducing it needs the page director and the twelve zone regions, which are not part of this component's evidence; the amendment deliberately records it as HomeTemplate's responsibility and captures nothing.

The rule exists only in page and component CSS (`.gl-on.gl-mob #slot-cap .fb3d{opacity:1}`, bundle.css line 49) and in the director's `applyMobileZones()`. The preview has no mobile state; capturing it would require fabricating markup.

Capturing the shipped React component requires the Storybook dev server, which is not authorized for this docs-only task. The v0.6 amendment changes no appearance, so no new implementation capture is requested; runtime visual conformity of the design system stays Not evaluated.

The web's reduced-motion poses are fixed values (`rm ? …`), already quoted in the approved v0.4 contract and covered by the existing reduced-motion tests; a static frame would add no information beyond VIS-05 and VIS-08.

limits: These images show the web's own preview composition and stage chrome (rounded stage, radial red wash). They are evidence for the inputs and pose families, never design-system tokens or approved expected design.
GPU rendering used SwiftShader software rasterisation through headless Chromium; lighting and anti-aliasing will differ from a hardware browser.

three@0.160.0 and the Google Fonts stylesheet were fetched from their original CDNs at capture time (200, no failed requests). A later run without network access would fall back to the SVG and produce different bytes; the hashes above identify the stored files only.
The preview's idle motion continues while capturing (brand-pixel drift and a small yaw sway), so a re-run may differ by a few pixels in the same conditions.

VIS-06 shows separated pieces clipped by the stage crop: the web fits the camera to assembled bounds, so progress-0 outro pieces fall outside the framing. This is an expected source behaviour, not a capture defect.
Browser images do not verify behaviour, accessibility, keyboard, focus or any design-system guarantee.

approval.reference: Pending: the owner approves or declines these captures as supporting evidence for Isotipo3D v0.6 in issue #47. Owner authorization for read-only Chromium capture under odd/tasks/web-catalog.md L6 covers the act of capturing, not adoption of these images as expected design.
